page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA extensions. It does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

A central characteristic of this instance is its constrained core configuration paired with a high memory allocation. The system supplies 512 GB of RAM, resulting in 16 GB of memory per vCPU. This architecture achieves a top-quartile PassMark memory score of 2,943.18, alongside read-only memory bandwidth measuring 2,072.44 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 77.51 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached transfers. Large block uncached memory write throughput measures 43.91 GB/sec. Local scratch storage is bundled as a 2,577 GB SSD, accommodating temporary data-intensive read/write operations without requiring remote disk roundtrips.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core throughput ranking in the upper 25% at 2,718.77. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50% tier across Geekbench (14,229.0 multi-core score) and PassMark CPU evaluations (38,454.81), corresponding to its 32-vCPU allocation. In synthetic application benchmarks, the instance delivers 31.93 million Redis SET operations per second and 23.59 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For CPU-bound machine learning tasks, small-model (135M) LLM text generation is robust at 318.51 tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly to 6.59 tokens per second for prompt processing on larger 70B models.

The E64-32ads_v5 offers favorable resource efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that simultaneously demands extensive memory space and fast local scratch storage. Primary target workloads include in-memory databases such as Redis, large relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, and memory-heavy batch processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high 16 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is provisioned via an integrated 2,577 GB SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted. Benchmark results highlight upper-quartile memory throughput and single-core stress-ng performance, complemented by 31.93 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-core processing aligns with median performance profiles for its core count. Because the instance restricts active vCPUs while retaining a full memory allotment, it offers efficient hardware utilization for software packages constrained by per-core licensing. The configuration is well suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches, and large ETL data processing pipelines.
